sections.label: SIAC 2019 case filings
sections.summary: In 2019 the SIAC reached 479 case filings, its third straight year above 400, with aims to improve.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2019, the SIAC saw a new high of 479 case filings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This is the third consecutive year that the SIAC's caseload has exceeded 400 and we will aim to do even better in the coming years.

sections.label: Default arbitrator appointment mechanism
sections.summary: After consulting stakeholders, the first proposal proceeds, setting a default mechanism for appointing arbitrators in multiparty situations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: After extensive consultation with stakeholders, we have decided to proceed with the first of the two of the proposals first.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, it sets out a default mechanism for the appointment of arbitrators in multiparty situations.

sections.label: Equal treatment in tribunal formation
sections.summary: The default procedure applies to three or more parties and three arbitrators only where parties have not agreed on appointment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We also want to ensure that, as far as possible, all parties receive equal treatment in the formation of the tribunal.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It will apply where there are three or more parties and three arbitrators.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The default procedure will only apply where parties have not agreed on a procedure for the appointment of the arbitrators.

sections.label: Appointing the presiding arbitrator
sections.summary: Two side-appointed arbitrators appoint the presiding third, but section 9B(2) lets the appointing authority appoint all three if parties disagree.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And finally, the two appointed arbitrators on both sides, will then get together and appoint the third arbitrator, who will be the presiding arbitrator.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: However, where parties are unable to come to an agreement on their choice of arbitrator, then the new section 9B(2) provides that the appointing authority must then, in that situation and upon the request of any party, appoint all three arbitrators.

sections.label: Default appointing authority under IAA
sections.summary: Under the IAA, absent party agreement, the default appointing authority is the SIAC Court of Arbitration President and Chief Justice nominees.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the IAA, where the parties have not agreed on who should be the appointing authority, then the default appointing authority will be the President of the Court of Arbitration of the SIAC and any other person nominated by the Chief Justice to exercise the powers of that appointing authority.

sections.label: Amendment enables expeditious tribunal constitution
sections.summary: The amendment ensures failure or refusal to agree on joint nominations will not prevent expeditious constitution of the arbitral tribunal.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: With the amendment, the parties' failure to agree on joint nominations, or indeed, a refusal to agree, will not prevent the arbitral tribunal from being constituted expeditiously.

sections.label: New IAA section 12(1)(j)
sections.summary: The Bill inserts a new section 12(1)(j) in the IAA to recognise powers of the arbitral tribunal and High Court to enforce that duty.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, seeks to insert a new section 12(1)(j) in the IAA to expressly recognise the powers of the arbitral tribunal and the High Court in terms of enforcing such a duty and to give effect to such obligations by making orders or giving directions as may be appropriate.

sections.label: Bill strengthens enforcement of confidentiality
sections.summary: The Bill does not codify confidentiality obligations but strengthens parties' ability to enforce existing ones, without requiring sealing or redaction applications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill, therefore, does not codify obligations of confidentiality but seeks to strengthen parties’ ability to enforce existing obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For instance, the new provision will not require a plaintiff in arbitration-related court proceedings, to have to apply for the sealing of the court file and redaction of the papers, when commencing such proceedings and that is the position currently.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It keeps us up to date and will ensure that Singapore remains an attractive venue for international arbitrations.

sections.label: Two key amendments in Bill
sections.summary: The Bill makes two key amendments: a default mode of appointing arbitrators in multi-party arbitrations and explicit enforcement of confidentiality obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This lends weight and legitimacy to the arbitration landscape in Singapore and parties can be confident that their earlier agreements to arbitrate their disputes will be upheld in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I understand that the Bill makes the following two key amendments: First, the introduction of a default mode of appointment of arbitrators in multi-party arbitrations where parties’ agreement does not specify the procedure for such appointments; and Second, the Bill will explicitly provide for the arbitral tribunal and the High Court to enforce obligations of confidentiality, by making the relevant and/or necessary orders and directions, where such obligations exist.

sections.label: Amendments plug lacuna in law
sections.summary: The amendments plug a lacuna in the law, and the stipulated appointment procedure should minimise procedural disputes, saving time and costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The amendments plug the lacuna in the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With the stipulated procedure on appointment of arbitrators in multi-party arbitrations, this should minimise procedural disputes on the same time, resulting in saved time and costs for parties.

sections.label: Statutory powers enforce confidentiality obligations
sections.summary: Statutory powers of the arbitral tribunal and High Court enforce existing confidentiality obligations under agreements or at law, giving them bite and effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The enactment of statutory powers of the arbitral tribunal and High Court to enforce existing confidentiality obligations, whether under agreements or at law, gives bite and effect to such obligations, which will certainly bring Singapore’s arbitration landscape to greater heights.

sections.label: Public consultation and first amendment
sections.summary: Six areas were put out for public consultation and the Bill implements two, the first being a default mode of appointment for arbitrators in multi-party arbitrations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Six areas were put out for public consultation and this Bill implements two of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The first amendment is to provide for a default mode of appointment for arbitrators in multi-party arbitrations.

sections.label: Confidentiality in arbitration proceedings
sections.summary: The second amendment addresses confidentiality, an issue it calls vexed, noting confidentiality obligations are common in arbitration proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The second amendment also deals with another vexed issue and this is confidentiality Confidentiality obligations are common in arbitration proceedings.

sections.label: Tribunal powers over confidentiality
sections.summary: The amendment to section 12 of the International Arbitration Act provides that the Tribunal has powers to make orders protecting confidentiality in an arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There was some debate on whether tribunals may have the power and to what extent that powers would extend to making confidentiality a part of the arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, by making this amendment to section 12 of the International Arbitration Act – which is really a section that spells out the Tribunal's powers – what it now provides specifically is that the Tribunal has such powers to make orders to protect confidentiality in an arbitration.

sections.label: Urging MinLaw to expedite proposals
sections.summary: The speaker urges MinLaw to expedite tabling other consultation paper proposals, describing an opt-in appeal to the High Court and an option to waive or limit annulment grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Corporations are also rethinking their agreements to prepare for a post-COVID world and considering the best dispute resolution mechanism that would offer them the best flexibility or option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, while I applaud the efforts made to further ensure that Singapore’s arbitration regime remains responsive and relevant to evolving needs, I would urge MinLaw to consider expediting the tabling of the other proposals in the consultation paper as this will be key to cementing Singapore’s status as the preferred seat for arbitration disputes and leapfrog us over other competitive jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The first of which would allow parties which seek greater curial intervention, to appeal to the High Court on a question of law in an award based on an opt-in mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The second would allow parties who on the other hand prefer minimal curial intervention, to agree to waive or limit the annulment grounds under the relevant sections of the IAA and the Model Law.

sections.label: Asking when proposals are tabled
sections.summary: The speaker seeks the Minister's indication on whether the other consultation paper proposals are being tabled and when, citing SIAC's 2019 record of 479 new case filings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There is an opportunity for us to reinvent and leapfrog the competition now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I therefore seek an indication from the Minister on whether the other proposals in the consultation paper, particularly the two I mentioned, are being tabled and if so, when.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Singapore International Arbitration Centre or SIAC set a new record with 479 new case filings and parties from over 59 jurisdictions chose Singapore as their destination for arbitration.

sections.label: Default appointment in multi-party situations
sections.summary: New section 9B details the default mode of appointment for multi-party situations, with concern about point 4 on the appointing authority appointing all three arbitrators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 9B details the default mode of appointment for multi-party situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is some concern about point 4 of this section, which states: if either the claimants or the respondents fail to appoint an arbitrator, the appointing authority must appoint all three arbitrators.

sections.label: Hong Kong statutory confidentiality duty
sections.summary: The Hong Kong Arbitration Ordinance expressly provides for a statutory duty of confidentiality in arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Hong Kong Arbitration Ordinance expressly provides for a statutory duty of confidentiality in arbitration.

sections.label: Reasoning against appeal right
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify why a right to appeal on a question of law was not included.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify the reasoning behind deciding against including this right to appeal on a question of law?

sections.label: Opt-in appeal on law
sections.summary: The opt-in mechanism lets parties choose to appeal on a question of law or rely on the default position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the opt-in mechanism allows parties to choose to exercise this right or to rely on the default position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This adds to Singapore’s commitment in giving parties the flexibility to determine certain issues and procedures in their arbitral proceedings, as compared to court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 49 of our Arbitration Act provides that a party to arbitral proceedings may, with the agreement of all parties and with the leave of the Court, appeal to the Court on a question of law arising out of an arbitral award.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Giving parties this option to have a right to appeal on a question of law may not only encourage more parties to arbitrate in Singapore, but also assist in determining case law in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support of the Bill.

sections.label: Institutional rules on tribunal designation
sections.summary: Most major institutional rules now permit or require institutions to designate the entire tribunal in multi-party proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Although the solutions adopted differ in some particulars, most major institutional rules, including the LCIA Arbitration Rules that Mr Louis Ng referred to, now either permit or, in fact, require the institutions to designate the entire tribunal in multi-party proceedings.

sections.label: Appointing authority discretion
sections.summary: The appointing authority may consider all relevant circumstances, including parties' antecedent conduct in choosing the arbitrator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And we are very much alive to that possibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, to allow the appointing authority some flexibility and the discretion to take into account what I have just articulated and, indeed, what Mr Louis Ng had put forward in his speech, the appointing authority is now clothed with the ability to look at all relevant circumstances and we do not define upfront what that might be precisely because it may differ from case to case and the antecedent conduct of the parties in terms of the choice of the arbitrator would be something that the appointing authority would look at.

sections.label: Appointing and confidentiality powers
sections.summary: The authority may reappoint or revoke appointments, and the tribunal and High Court may enforce confidentiality obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the context of appointing the three arbitrators, we have given broad remit to the authority to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have expressly said it may reappoint, meaning if one party has already chosen, it may reappoint, or it may decide to revoke the appointment altogether and decide afresh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the question of confidentiality, the amendment is to recognise that the tribunal and the High Court will have power to enforce these obligations.

sections.label: SIAC confidentiality scope and waivers
sections.summary: SIAC Rules stipulate confidentiality scope, and courts have found waivers including registered awards, party conduct and criminal conduct suspicion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To a reference that Mr Louis Ng brought up about institutional rules, I should add that the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) Rules do stipulate the scope of confidentiality and that it is stated to cover the existence of the proceedings itself, like the Hong Kong position that Mr Louis Ng mentioned – the pleadings, evidence and what other materials might arise in the context of the proceedings and, of course, all documents produced in discovery in those proceedings, and, finally, the award that was issued at the culmination of the proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Some examples of situations where the Courts have found that confidentiality obligations have been waived or where disclosure of confidential information is accepted include the following: (a) where the award is registered as a Singapore judgment and, obviously, it then enters into the realm of the public domain and privacy can no longer be attached to those proceedings and, therefore, the award itself; (b) alternatively, where parties have, by their own conduct, indicated for an agreement for the confidentiality to be waived, for example, by not requesting that an open Court proceeding in which confidential information is to be discussed or would be brought up in those proceedings, not requesting that those proceedings be heard in-camera; and (c) where there is reasonable suspicion of criminal conduct and there is a “public interest” behind why that information ought to be disclosed and an exception made for the confidential information arising out of the arbitration proceedings to be disclosed.

sections.label: Not codifying scope, courts decide
sections.summary: The decision was made against codifying the exact scope and application, leaving courts and the tribunal to assess case by case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is something that the High Court here in Singapore and also internationally have espoused.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, for that reason, we have decided against codifying and setting out the exact scope to what it applies and when it applies and let the Courts and the tribunal assess that question on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Opt-in appeal, annulment grounds studied
sections.summary: Other considerations on opt-in appeal and waiver or limitation of annulment grounds are still being studied and are not part of today's Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I have briefly outlined these other considerations earlier and they broadly relate to the opt-in right of appeal and the proposal for the waiver or limitation of the annulment grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These are still being studied and are not part of today's Bill, but I welcome Mr Vikram Nair's as well as Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim's views on them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We agree with the views that are set out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will add them on to the very many REACH views that we have received so far on this and study them together with the various stakeholders that I have mentioned at the outset.

sections.label: Operationalisation of mechanisms needs study
sections.summary: Operationalising these mechanisms needs study to ensure they are consistent and lend themselves to fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The operationalisation of these mechanisms also needs some study to ensure that they are consistent and that they lend themselves to fairness.
